A queue keeps a 24-byte ID after its 256 MiB receive buffer is reused. Which representation matches that ownership and retention policy?
Keep a slice into the reusable buffer
Copy the ID into a queue-owned value
Attach the whole buffer to every ID through Arc
Make the slice's lifetime parameter static

The queue needs independent ownership of the selected bytes. Copying the small field lets the receive buffer be reused. Shared ownership of the original allocation would preserve the bytes while retaining the entire allocation.
One branch moves a record's payload out of a plain struct. What can cleanup still destroy in that branch?
The complete original record, including its moved payload
Nothing from the record
Only its still-initialized fields
Only the fields that implement Copy

A partial move leaves the other initialized fields available for cleanup. The moved payload has a new owner. A type with its own Drop implementation imposes a different constraint because its destructor receives the whole value.
Two runtime indices differ and are in bounds. What lets safe Rust produce two simultaneous mutable references into a slice?
Checking the indices and splitting the slice into disjoint regions
Borrowing both indices in separate statements
Reserving capacity on the original vector
Adding the same lifetime to both references

The split exposes disjoint regions through the API. Index inequality is a fact about values, while the returned slice relationship gives the compiler a structure that supports simultaneous exclusive borrows.
A function owns a temporary record and calls a client closure. Which callback contract prevents the closure's result from borrowing that temporary?
Require the closure itself to live forever
Choose a lifetime parameter supplied by the client and return a reference with it
Move the record into an Arc and always return a clone
Use a for<'a> callback bound with a result type outside that binder

The callback must accept the short borrow chosen by the function. A result type outside the higher-ranked binder cannot depend on that borrow. It may still contain a reference obtained elsewhere with its own lifetime.
Why is &mut T invariant in T, even though the reference's own borrow lifetime can be shortened?
Every mutable reference stores a lifetime at runtime
A writable location could be filled with a shorter-lived value than its original owner permits
The compiler cannot represent nested lifetimes
All references are invariant in both parameters
If an exclusive slot of long-lived references could be viewed as a slot of short-lived references, a caller could store a short-lived value and later read it through the original stronger type.
A rollback guard temporarily changes a collection. A safe caller can forget the guard. Which invariant must still hold?
Rollback must still execute at scope exit
The original value must be restored exactly
The remaining collection must be safe to access or destroy
The caller must receive a compile error

Rust permits a safe caller to leak a guard. The ordinary rollback promise can depend on running Drop, but memory safety must survive a forgotten guard. Keep the observable state valid throughout the operation.
A RefCell-based document invokes a callback that can edit the same document. Which plan handles both reentrancy and stale proposals?
Snapshot the input, release the borrow, then validate the generation before committing
Hold RefMut throughout so the callback sees a consistent view
Use borrow instead of borrow_mut for the entire operation
Replace every borrow with try_borrow and accept any successful proposal

A short borrow avoids conflicting runtime borrows during the callback. The generation check addresses a separate logical problem. A proposal can become stale even when all dynamic borrow checks succeed.
An arena recycles an index after deletion. What stops an old ID from naming the new occupant?
Keeping all records in one Vec
Giving the index a newtype
Checking whether the index is in bounds
Comparing a stored generation as well as the slot
A generation distinguishes successive occupants of a slot. In-bounds checks alone only confirm storage exists. Cross-arena identity and counter exhaustion need separate policies.
A planner chooses one output type per implementation, and each policy can support several plan types. How should the relationships be expressed?
Make both output and policy generic methods
Use an associated output on the planner and a plan type parameter on the policy
Erase all plans to Any
Require every plan to implement Display

The associated type records the output selected by the planner implementation. The policy parameter allows one policy type to have several independent implementation relationships. Reporting bounds belong on operations that report.
A function changes from &mut T where T: Sink to &mut dyn Sink. Which property necessarily changes at that interface?
The sink must move to the heap
The sink must become Send
The interface uses an erased receiver instead of a caller-selected concrete type
The reference owns the sink
The erased reference carries access to the sink and dispatch metadata. The same sink can still live in a caller's local storage. Allocation, thread transfer, and ownership are separate choices.
An upstream crate has a blanket trait implementation covering your local type. Why can a second implementation still be rejected?
Coherence rejects overlapping implementations even when the orphan rule allows your local type
Any implementation for a local type overrides a blanket implementation
The method names collide at runtime
Only implementations in the standard library can be generic
Local ownership can satisfy the orphan rules. The implementation still overlaps with the blanket implementation. A wrapper or another explicit implementation relationship can make the cases distinct.
A move closure captures a Vec and returns its length on every call. What determines whether it can implement Fn?
Whether the closure uses move
Whether the Vec implements Copy
Whether the caller stores it on the heap
Whether calling the body only needs shared access to captured state
Move controls how the vector enters the environment. Calling len borrows that environment, so owning the captured value does not force the closure to consume it during a call.
A reader reuses one buffer and yields views into it. How can its trait express that a view must be released before the next read?
Use Iterator<Item = &'static str>
Tie a GAT view lifetime to each borrow of the receiver
Return a raw pointer as the associated item
Use a longer lifetime parameter on the buffer type
The view belongs to the current receiver borrow, so a later mutable read must wait until that view is no longer used. Ordinary Iterator has one item type independent of a particular next call.
A remote operation times out after the request was sent. What should a structured error preserve?
A guarantee that nothing happened
Only a human-readable error string
An unknown-outcome category and the operation identity
A fresh identifier for an automatic retry

Timeout leaves the peer's commit status uncertain. Preserve the original identity and use the peer's status or idempotency protocol to resolve it. A local error alone provides no remote rollback evidence.
An approved dispatch ticket owns a payload. Which failure can safely return the same approval for reuse under the described protocol?
A local capacity rejection before handoff
A lost acknowledgement after the peer may have accepted it
A confirmed receipt
Every error that happens before returning to the caller

Pre-handoff rejection preserves the original local permission. After a possible handoff, return an uncertainty state carrying the operation identity. That state needs a reconciliation policy instead of blind redispatch.
A private field becomes non-Send in a public registry type. Which downstream behavior can break?
Only callers that name the field
No behavior because the field is private
Only the Debug output
Moving the registry to a worker thread

Auto traits are observable at the API boundary. A private representation change can remove Send and break a downstream bound. Keep a small client compile check for the transfer capability you intend to support.
An exported macro expands a user expression into two uses of the expression itself. What is the repair when it must evaluate exactly once?
Add Clone to the expression type
Bind the expression once inside the expansion and use the binding
Wrap each occurrence in a block
Make the expansion procedural
A local binding gives the expression one evaluation and makes ownership of its result visible. A macro test with a side-effecting, non-Copy value exposes accidental reevaluation.
Cartridge<CAP> accepts variable-length inputs up to CAP. Where should the actual used length live?
In a new type for each runtime message
In a build-script constant
In a checked runtime field beside the fixed-capacity storage
In size_of::<usize>() on the build host

The type parameter captures capacity known at compile time. A runtime counter records what the input actually occupies. Keep wire-format bounds and header arithmetic explicit and independent of the build host.
A scoped worker returns Vec<&str> built from its borrowed catalog partition. What does the output borrow?
The caller's catalog storage
The temporary Vec allocation itself
The worker stack frame
The join handle

The worker's vector owns reference values. The strings remain owned by the caller, so returned references retain the catalog's lifetime. Joining establishes the worker boundary, while the borrow relation preserves validity after it.
A condition variable wakes a thread waiting for a snapshot revision. What establishes readiness?
The notification count
The fact that the thread acquired a CPU
The absence of mutex poisoning
The protected revision predicate checked again under the lock
The condition variable helps wait efficiently. The stored state is authoritative. Rechecking the predicate under the mutex handles early, irrelevant, and spurious wakes.
A bounded fanout enqueues to recipient A, then recipient B disconnects. What should the relay report?
Both sends failed as one transaction
A accepted the queue transfer, B did not, and processing remains separate
A processed the payload durably
B can be retried only after issuing a different operation ID to A
Separate sends create separate acceptance events. B's failure returns its undelivered value without undoing A's accepted send. Processing and durability require their own acknowledgements.
A release store publishes a flag after a payload write. When does an acquire load of the flag supply the intended publication edge?
Whenever it is executed on another thread
When it returns the old value
When it observes the publication through the relevant synchronization relation
Only when the payload is also sequentially consistent

The reader needs an actual synchronizing observation. An acquire operation that sees an older state does not acquire the new publication. The proof follows the events involved in the specific handoff.
A CPU-work future consumes one chunk and returns Pending while more chunks are already available. What must it arrange?
Another poll, such as by waking the current task
A new OS thread for each chunk
A successful final result hidden inside Pending
A borrowed reference to its own buffer stored across polls

A pending future needs a path back to polling. If work is immediately available, a wake can request another poll while the future yields its budget. This is distinct from guaranteeing fairness across executor tasks.
A parent future stores Pin<Box<Child>>. What moves when the parent moves?
The address-sensitive Child inside the allocation
Neither the handle nor the parent
Only Child's fields
The pinned box handle, while its pointee stays in place
Pinning constrains movement of the pointee. The owning pointer can move without extracting the child. Taking or dropping a pinned box handle can therefore be sound even when the child is not Unpin.
A one-shot receiver sees no value and wants to return Pending. Which protocol closes the lost-wake gap?
Check once, unlock, then store a waker
Check state and register the waker under one synchronization discipline
Count wake calls and use that count as the result
Use the first waker forever

A coordinated check and registration ensures either the receiver sees the published state or the sender sees the registered waker. Store terminal state even when nobody is waiting, and refresh the waker when the polling context changes.
A borrowed write future can be dropped after writing a partial frame. Where should indispensable resume state live?
Only in local variables of the future
In the waker
In the connection or exporter that survives the future
In a Drop routine that awaits the peer

The resource owner keeps the frame and acknowledged offset after the attempt is dropped. A subsequent operation resumes from that state or explicitly aborts. Local byte progress does not settle remote commit status.
A scanner is Sync and its method borrows a request. Which additional property must a generic caller see if it needs to move the operation across threads?
A Send bound on the returned future
A guarantee that the returned report is borrowed
A static annotation on every argument
An Unpin bound on the scanner's trait object

Scanner Sync describes shared access to the scanner. The future can retain other values across suspension. Publish its Send promise in the interface, and handle the separate static lifetime requirement at an unscoped task boundary.
A supervisor sent cancellation to a worker. Which evidence establishes that the worker actually stopped?
The cancellation flag was set
A timeout elapsed
The input queue reached zero
The supervisor observed termination through the owned completion handle
Cancellation asks a worker to stop. Observing its completion establishes local termination. The supervisor still needs a separate classification for a remote side effect whose outcome is uncertain.
A network header must have the same seven-byte representation on every target. Which design establishes that contract?
Transmute a repr(C) struct to bytes
Encode fields explicitly with fixed widths and chosen byte order
Use size_of::<Header>() as the protocol header length
Serialize the address of a header instance

A wire protocol needs explicit byte positions, widths, and endianness. A layout annotation gives particular in-memory guarantees and does not by itself define a portable encoding or validate incoming data.
Two raw pointers contain the same numeric address. What additional evidence is needed before dereferencing one?
The integer is nonzero
The same address appeared in a previous allocation
Appropriate provenance, live storage, alignment, validity, and compatible access
The pointer was loaded with acquire ordering

Numeric identity is insufficient. The operation needs authority to access the relevant live allocation and must meet alignment, initialized value, and aliasing requirements. Ordering does not extend allocation lifetime.
A safe API uses unsafe unchecked UTF-8 conversion after promising ASCII-only contents. What must be true of every safe mutation path?
It must preserve or reestablish the valid-byte invariant before any unchecked view
It must use a private method name
It may rely on the caller reading the docs
It may temporarily expose invalid bytes as str if tests pass

A safe caller must be unable to trigger undefined behavior, including after errors, panics, or forgotten guards. The unchecked conversion relies on a representation invariant that each safe path must uphold.
A sparse builder initializes slots out of order in MaybeUninit storage. What determines which destructors must run?
The largest index ever written
The allocation's byte capacity
Whether T is Copy
A record of precisely which slots hold live initialized values

An initialized prefix counter only works when initialization is contiguous. Sparse writes need a separate map or equivalent invariant. Update that state in the correct order when taking, replacing, or destroying an element.
A foreign caller receives an opaque Rust-owned handle. Which function should destroy it?
The caller's free function for any pointer-shaped value
The Rust export paired with the allocation and its documented ownership protocol
Any function that calls Drop on a copied handle
A function inferred from the handle's numeric address

The paired destructor uses the same allocation and ownership representation as the constructor. The interface must specify exactly-once release and which thread or callback obligations survive until release.
Two indexes reference a record in a dense archive. Swap-removing the record moves another record. What must change?
Only the dense Vec length
The moved record's logical identity
Every index entry that tracks the moved record's physical position
Nothing if the old position is still in bounds
Physical location and logical identity are different. Repair the moved record's position mappings while preserving its stable identity, and make deletion and reuse invalidate any obsolete handles.
A benchmark claims erased dispatch is slower, but only the erased version allocates every record. What should change first?
Equalize representation and allocation work before attributing a difference to dispatch
Add more iterations to the same setup
Remove output validation
Assume the optimizer removes all allocations
The experiment changes multiple variables at once. Isolate dispatch with comparable work, check that both variants produce equivalent outputs, and measure the allocation policy separately.
A model test finds a failing event sequence. What makes it a durable regression artifact?
The number of random cases generated
Only the final assertion message
A passing run with a different seed
A reproducible sequence, the expected invariant, and the observed violation
Keep a reduced event sequence and precise invariant so the failure can be replayed. A model, fuzz run, or interpreter check contributes evidence for the cases it explores.
A parser returns views that need to outlive a mutable input buffer's reuse. Which redesign enables that?
Keep borrowing the buffer and call reserve
Own the retained bytes or retain an independent immutable backing owner
Use an unchecked lifetime extension
Make every view a byte offset without retaining any backing bytes
A view needs backing storage that remains valid. Owning selected fields or owning an immutable snapshot with validated ranges both establish that relationship. An offset alone does not own the bytes.
Two independent stores have the same numeric version. What must a transaction validate before commit?
Only the version number
Only that its change map is nonempty
That the snapshot belongs to the target state as well as matching its version
That keys are stored in lexical order
Equal revisions do not identify a store. A current-map identity check or explicit store identity prevents applying a transaction's decisions to a different origin with the same version.
The collector in a bounded worker pipeline fails while workers are blocked on output. Which shutdown fact matters first?
Ensure blocked senders can observe the receiver closure or continue to drain
Increase the output buffer until the next test passes
Join workers while keeping every receiver alive and unread
Count a failed send as proof an earlier job did not execute

Workers need a path out of blocked sends before the supervisor waits for them. Undelivered result transfer is a different event from executing the associated job. Account for accepted jobs separately.
A client loses the acknowledgement after dispatch. Which transition preserves the protocol's uncertainty?
Reset to Ready and forget the old identifier
Mark Delivered because the socket accepted bytes
Mark Failed and imply the peer had no effect
Enter Unknown with the original operation identity
The local transport event does not establish what the peer committed. Preserve the operation identity and resolve the unknown outcome through the peer's deduplication or status contract.
Two downstream crates enable different features of a shared dependency. What design reduces feature-unification surprises?
Rely on each dependent keeping its own independent build
Make capabilities additive or choose incompatible policies explicitly at runtime
Enable every feature in build.rs and hide it from callers
Use incompatible definitions with the same name under every combination

Features often combine across dependency users. Additive capabilities have a defined combined meaning. Where policies are exclusive, separate packages or explicit values can represent that choice more reliably.
A final design passes every unit test. Which additional artifact makes its most important guarantees reviewable?
A count of lines of Rust
A claim that the type checker covers every failure
A ledger tying each invariant to its owner, failure evidence, and protocol boundary
A screenshot of the terminal test output

A reviewer needs to see who owns each obligation and what would falsify it. Type checks, runtime tests, and external protocols supply different evidence. Connect each claim to the right evidence and name the limits.
